findings.message: Saves stop working after a reload. When a career is loaded, decode → validateWorld moves `w.sponsor` into `sponsors[local|shirt]` and deletes `w.sponsor`, and the host keeps that migrated world in memory. The engine still only checks `w.sponsor`, so it signs a second sponsor: at level 4 delegatedBusiness does it the next clubDay; otherwise the season-start reminder shows the slot as empty and the owner signs again. The next checkpoint() then encodes → decodes → legacySponsor moves the new sponsor into the same slot, and the load fails with '후원 계약 손상' (schema.contract.test.ts:206-209 asserts exactly this throw). The codec writes nothing on failure, so that career never saves again on the group branch. The T051 result's limits only say the migrated contract goes unpaid. Fix: until T056, the legacy sponsor paths in ops-commercial.ts (delegatedBusiness, sponsorReminder, the `sponsor` command guard, the exclusive-merchandise check) should treat a contract in `w.sponsors` as the club's sponsor, so `sponsor` and `sponsors` never exist together. Add a regression test: decode a sponsored 1.15 world with business delegated, advance a day, and check that checkpoint/encode→decode still succeeds.

Two checks break, and no task owns either file. The benchmark's active-management profile signs through `sponsor`, and measure() calls `validateWorld(w)` without a catalog, which now throws ('이전 규칙의 후원 계약을 옮길 카탈로그가 없습니다'); the lossless decode comparison would fail too. CI's benchmark job runs `pnpm run benchmark`. The sponsor-installment e2e journey expects `signed.sponsor` on a decoded world, which `pnpm run verify` (the group verify) runs. The T051 result lists both failures, but T056's touches include neither file and T062's does not include the benchmark, so they would stay red at group verify. Fix the benchmark here (pass LOAD_CATALOG and compare against the migrated world, or stop signing through `sponsor`). Either fix business.spec.ts here or record an explicit hand-off so the planner adds both files to T056/T062's touches.

The cash remedy sheet still offers 'support-down' (선수단 투자 one level lower) as a way to stretch cash. Since the wage multiplier was removed, that saves nothing and only costs development and recovery, which is wrong advice during a bankruptcy countdown (WEB-44 remedies must state their real cost and effect). PolicyBoard's support dial also now always shows 연간 운영비 +0. No task in the group touches teamState.ts. Remove or replace this cash remedy in this lane and adjust its test. Otherwise, record the gap for the planner to assign alongside T058/T057.

Existing saves keep their delegation, so every career saved before this change now shows a custom (맞춤) intervention level until the owner picks a level again. This follows the spec (WEB-45), but the owner sees it immediately. Whether a load should delegate `contracts` for clubs at level 2 and up is a planning decision; hand it to the planner. The e2e STOP_KINDS list also lacks the four new inbox kinds; T053's e2e pass could add them.

The T051 and T052 results record `at: -` instead of the commits they were verified at (3d35c16, d2312dd). T051's acceptance checkbox names `hire-manager`, but the implementation adds `term` to `hire` instead. That follows STAFF-17 and the result explains it; keep it noted for the staff lane (T060/T061).

reviewHistory.summary: T054 meets its acceptance. The client records the three app notices as `{id,text,at,read}` system notifications in `haeram-soccor:notifications`, kept in the browser and never in the world. The inbox lists them as 시스템, counts them as unread until the opened inbox closes, and they never stop the clock. The banner is gone, and the unit tests cover the upgrade-once and read-persists cases. T053's notation work is mostly sound. `compactMoney` matches T052's moneyLabel cases, the HUD uses the notation on every viewport, and affordability checks still compare exact BigInt amounts. T053 has one real gap, though. At the bid step and staff-hiring decisions, amounts were changed to bare `compactMoney` text with no exact value anywhere, so the owner can no longer see the exact fee or wage before committing. That breaks WEB-67 ('the exact amount opens on tap or hover') and acceptance 1, even though `<Money plain>` was written for exactly this case. Coverage: I read the code and did not run any checks. The task results record runs only through the unit tests: the coordinator ran Chromium e2e on 1c96d71 for T053, and T054's recovery.spec change was never run. The group verify (`pnpm run verify`, which includes test:e2e) still has to confirm it.

findings.message: The bid dialog's percentage steps and the '… 제안 보내기' button now show only `compactMoney` text, with no title and no tap. The exact fee being offered is shown nowhere in the dialog (only the asking fee and the cash after go through `<Money>`). The baseline showed it exactly. This breaks WEB-67 ('the exact amount opens on tap or hover') and acceptance 1, and `Money.tsx` documents `plain` as being for 'a radio step, a confirm button'. Fix: render these amounts with `<Money … plain />`, which keeps the notation and adds the exact title without nesting a button. Extend recruitment.spec to check the exact title on a bid step.

The staff candidate radio (연봉/계약금) and the DepartmentDial step wages (`stepCost` returns a string) now show only `compactMoney` text. The hire confirmation shows only the candidate's name, so the exact wage and fee of a staff hire can no longer be seen anywhere. Fix: use `<Money plain>` inside the radio, and let `stepCost` return a ReactNode with `<Money plain>` so each step carries the exact title. Change T053's acceptance 1 from [v] to unmet until this is done.

Amounts built into strings (policy dial previews, remedy choices, outcome cards, stance consequences, chart bubbles) carry the notation with no exact disclosure. T053's limits declare this, but WEB-67 does not say whether amounts inside sentences are exempt. Planning (update-ssot WEB-67) should decide whether sentence amounts may be notation-only or need ReactNode lines with `<Money plain>`. This review does not decide that.

`result.recovered` stays true on every load until the next commit moves the manifest off the corrupt slot. Reloading a recovered writer tab before any save therefore adds another unread '이전의 정상 체크포인트로 복구했습니다.' each time, and unread notices are never pruned. Consider skipping an add when an unread notice with the same text is already stored, or notifying a recovery only once per manifest generation.

The Web Locks warning still sets `state.notice` with `readonly` false. Its only display was the removed banner, and `ReadonlyBadge` renders only for read-only tabs, so the warning is now never shown. T054's result says `state.notice` 'explains the read-only badge (… or no Web Locks)', which is wrong for this branch. In practice the branch is close to unreachable, since every browser with CompressionStream and crypto.subtle also has Web Locks. Either correct the result text or route the warning to the badge or a system notification (a planning call under WEB-66).

Both tasks add to the entry bundle (the Money component and the notification store plus inbox rows). The entry had about 6.4 KB of headroom (249,558 of 256,000 bytes per the WEB r49 log), and `pnpm run benchmark:browser` was not measured. Only the CI benchmark job checks this, so the coordinator should confirm the entry stays within entryGzipLimit before the lane merges.

findings.message: Saves stop working after a reload. When a career is loaded, decode → validateWorld moves `w.sponsor` into `sponsors[local|shirt]` and deletes `w.sponsor`, and the host keeps that migrated world in memory. The engine still only checks `w.sponsor`, so it signs a second sponsor: at level 4 delegatedBusiness does it the next clubDay; otherwise the season-start reminder shows the slot as empty and the owner signs again. The next checkpoint() then encodes → decodes → legacySponsor moves the new sponsor into the same slot, and the load fails with '후원 계약 손상' (schema.contract.test.ts:206-209 asserts exactly this throw). The codec writes nothing on failure, so that career never saves again on the group branch. The T051 result's limits only say the migrated contract goes unpaid. Fix: until T056, the legacy sponsor paths in ops-commercial.ts (delegatedBusiness, sponsorReminder, the `sponsor` command guard, the exclusive-merchandise check) should treat a contract in `w.sponsors` as the club's sponsor, so `sponsor` and `sponsors` never exist together. Add a regression test: decode a sponsored 1.15 world with business delegated, advance a day, and check that checkpoint/encode→decode still succeeds.

Two checks break, and no task owns either file. The benchmark's active-management profile signs through `sponsor`, and measure() calls `validateWorld(w)` without a catalog, which now throws ('이전 규칙의 후원 계약을 옮길 카탈로그가 없습니다'); the lossless decode comparison would fail too. CI's benchmark job runs `pnpm run benchmark`. The sponsor-installment e2e journey expects `signed.sponsor` on a decoded world, which `pnpm run verify` (the group verify) runs. The T051 result lists both failures, but T056's touches include neither file and T062's does not include the benchmark, so they would stay red at group verify. Fix the benchmark here (pass LOAD_CATALOG and compare against the migrated world, or stop signing through `sponsor`). Either fix business.spec.ts here or record an explicit hand-off so the planner adds both files to T056/T062's touches.

The cash remedy sheet still offers 'support-down' (선수단 투자 one level lower) as a way to stretch cash. Since the wage multiplier was removed, that saves nothing and only costs development and recovery, which is wrong advice during a bankruptcy countdown (WEB-44 remedies must state their real cost and effect). PolicyBoard's support dial also now always shows 연간 운영비 +0. No task in the group touches teamState.ts. Remove or replace this cash remedy in this lane and adjust its test. Otherwise, record the gap for the planner to assign alongside T058/T057.

Existing saves keep their delegation, so every career saved before this change now shows a custom (맞춤) intervention level until the owner picks a level again. This follows the spec (WEB-45), but the owner sees it immediately. Whether a load should delegate `contracts` for clubs at level 2 and up is a planning decision; hand it to the planner. The e2e STOP_KINDS list also lacks the four new inbox kinds; T053's e2e pass could add them.
